docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Welcome to CloudBridge! Multiple clouds, one Kotlin Multiplatform bridge. Supporting Android, iOS, web and desktop (JVM).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The library is published to Maven Central.

dependencies {
    implementation("nl.jacobras:cloudbridge:0.15.0")
}

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
In general, CloudBridge works as follows:

// 1: Instantiate a service
val service = CloudBridge.dropbox(clientId = "yourClientId")

// 2: Authenticate (platform- and service-specific, see docs)
service.authenticate(redirectUri = "example://redirect-uri")

// 3: Ready for use!
val items = service.listFiles("/".asFolderPath()).items

See Cloud services on how to authenticate each service on every platform.

See shared API for all available operations.

See the demo app source for more example code.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: listFiles() is now paged. It takes an optional cursor and returns a ListResult with items and a nextCursor (null on the last page). Pages hold up to about 200 items. See Listing files.
  • Dropbox and OneDrive now also set prompt=consent, like Google Drive, so a user can choose the desired account when connecting.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• completeAuthentication() on Android and web now throw CloudBridgeException instead of raw Ktor exceptions.
  • OneDrive's listFiles() now returns correct relative paths (fixes #18).
  • listFiles() on Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive silently dropped items beyond the first page (100 items on Google Drive, 200 on OneDrive). These can now be fetched with nextCursor.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• maxConcurrentWrites to RateLimiter. Only set by Dropbox for now (to 1), to fix excessive rate limiting (#124).
  • Logger.warn(message, throwable), used for failures like authentication errors. Defaults to log(); override it to log at warning level (#128).
  • NotAuthenticatedException now has the underlying error as cause (like the service's response with invalid_grant) (#128).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Breaking: renamed SetupException to ServiceSetupException (#127).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Linking Google Drive on Android no longer fails with NotAuthenticatedException when Google Identity Services returns a cached access token that Google no longer accepts. The token is cleared and authorization is requested once more (#128).
  • Google Drive file revisions are now based on md5Checksum instead of version, which also changes on server-side changes outside the library (for example right after every upload) (#125).
  • WebDAV folder IDs no longer end with a trailing slash, so they're the same whether the server adds one (#127).
  • WebDAV createFolder now throws ConflictException instead of Unknown when the folder already exists (#127).
  • WebDAV moves throw new WebDavMoveException instead of Unknown when the server rejects MOVE with 405 or 501 (#127).
  • WebDAV moves and createFolder throw NotFoundException instead of Unknown when the (destination's) parent folder doesn't exist (#127).

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: CloudBridge aims to make it easy to support multiple cloud services in your app, without having to go learn every detail of each specific service.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: The library only supports limited/private app folders, no full access.

docs.title: Paths and IDs
docs.text: The library prefers to work with IDs over paths.

docs.title: Strongly typed
docs.text: id and path variables are typed as much as possible, to prevent accidental mix-ups.

docs.title: Unified error handling
docs.text:
Dropbox will throw 409 when it can't find a path. Other services throw 404. CloudBridge turns them both into CloudBridgeException.NotFoundException. The same for all other errors, see Errors for an overview.

Feel free to open an issue if you have a different use case for any of these.

docs.title: Checking authentication
docs.text:
val service = CloudBridge.dropbox(clientId = "yourClientId", token = token)

if (service.isAuthenticated()) {
    // Ready to use.
}

Call setToken() to attach or replace the access token used for authentication, for example after loading a previously stored token:

service.setToken(storedToken)

docs.title: Token refresh
docs.text:
CloudBridge refreshes tokens automatically. You only need to store the updated token after it's been refreshed:

val service = CloudBridge.dropbox(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    token = storedToken,
    onTokenRefreshed = { token -> TODO("Store the token locally") }
)

The token is refreshed 1 minute before it expires (see CloudAccessToken.expiresAt). If a request still fails with an authentication error, the token is refreshed and the request is retried once. If refreshing fails (for example, because the user revoked access), a NotAuthenticatedException is thrown and the user needs to re-authenticate.

Note

Google Drive doesn't support refreshing tokens on web. See Google Drive for details.

docs.title: Getting user info
docs.text:
try {
    val userInfo = service.getUserInfo()
    println(userInfo.name)
    println(userInfo.emailAddress)
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: All suspending calls can throw a CloudBridgeException.

docs.title: Common exceptions
docs.text:
These are expected in normal use.

Exception Cause CloudBridgeException.ConflictException An item with the same name already exists CloudBridgeException.ConnectionException A network error occurred CloudBridgeException.InsufficientSpaceException The account has no storage space left CloudBridgeException.NotAuthenticatedException The service has no valid access token (yet) CloudBridgeException.NotFoundException The requested item could not be found CloudBridgeException.RateLimitException A rate limit was hit

docs.title: Less common exceptions
docs.text:
These are not expected to happen during normal use.

Exception Cause CloudBridgeException.IllegalArgumentException An argument is invalid, e.g. a missing or wrong sizeInBytes for a large OneDrive upload CloudBridgeException.ServiceSetupException The service is set up wrong, usually in its cloud console or admin panel CloudBridgeException.SinkWriteException Writing the download to the Sink failed CloudBridgeException.SourceReadException Reading the Source to upload failed, or it was already read CloudBridgeException.WebDavMoveException The WebDAV server rejects MOVE (HTTP 405/501), so items can't be moved or renamed CloudBridgeException.Unknown Any other unexpected error

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Files and folders are addressed with FilePath and FolderPath, both of which always start with a slash. Create them with the asFilePath() / asFolderPath() extension functions:

val file = "/Projects/welcome.txt".asFilePath()
val folder = "/Projects".asFolderPath()
val root = "/".asFolderPath()

docs.title: Listing files
docs.text:
Lists files and folders one level deep; nested content is not fetched. Results are paged: each call returns one page of up to about 200 items, plus a nextCursor to fetch the next page with. nextCursor is null when there are no more pages.

try {
    val result = service.listFiles("/".asFolderPath())
    val items = result.items
    val nextCursor = result.nextCursor // null if this was the last page
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

To fetch all items, keep calling listFiles() with the same path and the previous nextCursor:

val items = mutableListOf<CloudItem>()
var cursor: ListCursor? = null
do {
    val page = service.listFiles(path, cursor)
    items += page.items
    cursor = page.nextCursor
} while (cursor != null)
  • A page can hold fewer items than the page size. Google Drive can even return an empty page that still has a nextCursor, so always check nextCursor instead of the number of items.
  • WebDAV has no paging, so it returns all items at once with a null cursor.

docs.title: Listing delta changes
docs.text:
Lists all file/folder changes since the last time this was called. Not supported by all services, see Cloud services for the support matrix.

try {
    val result = service.getDelta(previousCursor)
    val previousCursor = result.newCursor
    val changes = result.changes
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

Unlike listFiles(), getDelta() isn't paged: all pages of changes are fetched internally and returned in one result. On large accounts, the first call (with DeltaCursor.INITIAL) can therefore take a while.

docs.title: Getting file or folder info
docs.text:
Fetches the metadata of a single file or folder. If nothing exists at the path, or the item has the other type (a folder when asking for a file or the other way round), a NotFoundException is thrown.

try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.getFileInfo("/Projects/Welcome.txt".asFilePath())
    val folder: CloudFolder = service.getFolderInfo("/Projects".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

Calling getFolderInfo() for the root folder (/) throws an IllegalArgumentException.

docs.title: Creating a folder
docs.text:
try {
    service.createFolder("/Projects".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Creating a text file
docs.text:
try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.createFile("/Projects/Welcome.txt".asFilePath(), "Hello world!")
    println("Created ${file.id} at revision ${file.revision}")
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Updating a text file
docs.text:
try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.updateFile(fileId, "Updated content")
    println("Updated ${file.id} to revision ${file.revision}")
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Uploading binary or large files
docs.text:
For images, archives and other binary content, pass a function that opens a kotlinx.io.Source. Files larger than 10 MB are automatically uploaded in chunks1.

try {
    val localPath = Path("photo.jpg")
    service.createFile(
        path = localPath.name.asFilePath(),
        source = { SystemFileSystem.source(localPath).buffered() },
        sizeInBytes = SystemFileSystem.metadataOrNull(localPath)?.size,
        mimeType = "image/jpeg",
        onProgress = { bytesSent, totalBytes -> println("Sent $bytesSent of $totalBytes bytes") }
    )
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}
  • The function is called once per attempt, so an upload can be retried after rate limiting. It must return a new Source at the start of the content each time. A CloudBridgeException.SourceReadException is thrown if it returns a source that was already read.
  • Each source is read until its end and then closed by the library.
  • sizeInBytes is optional, except for OneDrive files larger than 10 MB (throws a CloudBridgeException.IllegalArgumentException if missing or not matching the content size in that case).
  • mimeType defaults to application/octet-stream. Dropbox doesn't store MIME types and ignores it.
  • onProgress is optional and useful to track how far uploads are progressing. totalBytes is sizeInBytes if given, otherwise only known after the last chunk.
  • WebDAV has no chunked uploads, so the content is streamed in a single request and onProgress is called once, when done.
  • updateFile() has as similar signature as createFile().

docs.title: Using an InputStream
docs.text:
Here's an example on how to use an InputStream on Android and desktop:

try {
    val file = File("photo.jpg")
    service.createFile(
        path = file.name.asFilePath(),
        source = { file.inputStream().asSource().buffered() },
        sizeInBytes = file.length(),
        mimeType = "image/jpeg"
    )
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Downloading a file
docs.text:
try {
    val content: String = service.downloadFile(fileId)
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Downloading binary or large files
docs.text:
For images, archives and other binary content, pass a kotlinx.io.Sink. The content is streamed into it, so large files aren't held in memory. The sink is flushed, but not closed.

try {
    SystemFileSystem.sink(Path("photo.jpg")).buffered().use { sink ->
        service.downloadFile(fileId, sink)
    }
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

To get the content in memory instead, use a Buffer:

val buffer = Buffer()
service.downloadFile(fileId, buffer)
val bytes = buffer.readByteArray()

docs.title: Moving or renaming a file or folder
docs.text:
To rename an item, move it within the same folder. If an item already exists at the new path, a CloudBridgeException.ConflictException is thrown.

try {
    // Rename/move a file
    service.moveFile(fileId, "/Projects/New name.txt".asFilePath())

    // Or a folder
    service.moveFolder(folderId, "/Projects2".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

On WebDAV, the id of an item is its path, so the returned item has a new id.

docs.title: Deleting a file or folder
docs.text:
try {
    service.delete(itemId)
} catch (e: CloudBridgeException) {
    // Handle...
}

  1. Chunk size is around 10 MB, which is "optimal for stable high speed connections" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession?view=graph-rest-1.0#best-practices). See the support matrix for details. ↩

docs.title: API
docs.text:
First, authenticate the service you wish to use (see Services). Once authenticated, every service exposes the same shared API described in this section.

There may be differences, see Cloud services for the support matrix.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
CloudBridge uses rate limiting, so you can make as many calls as you like.

Here are the default (non-changeable) settings:

Service Max. concurrent requests Max. requests per second Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive 5 5.0 WebDAV 10 10.0

The limits count HTTP requests, so a chunked upload counts separately. The limits are shared per service, so, for example, multiple accounts to Dropbox will together do max 5 concurrent requests.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text:
A service can still respond with a rate limit, depending on internal rules at the cloud providers. Requests are automatically retried up to 3 times, backing off exponentially.

A CloudBridgeException.RateLimitException is thrown, with retryAfter (if provided), when:

  • The retries are exhausted.
  • The service asks to wait longer than 30 seconds.

A retried binary upload calls the source param passed to createFile() or updateFile() again. See uploading binary or large files.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
These are the non-configurable defaults set by CloudBridge.

Timeout Limit Description connect 20 seconds Connection should happen within this time. socket 20 seconds Longest wait time for new bytes during a request. request 2 minutes Maximum total duration of a request.

docs.title: ☁️ Dropbox
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.dropbox(clientId = "yourClientId")

Then, authenticate using the platform-specific methods below. Once authenticated, the shared API is available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Path case insensitivity

Dropbox paths are case-insensitive, meaning /Folder/File.txt and /folder/file.txt refer to the same file.

docs.title: Authenticating
☁️ Google Drive
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.googleDrive(clientId = "yourClientId")

On desktop, also pass the client secret. This is provided in the Google Drive API console when you create a desktop client.

CloudBridge.googleDrive(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    desktopClientSecret = "yourSecret"
)

On Android, the client ID isn't used (Google Identity Services identifies the app by its package name and signing certificate), so any value works.

Then, authenticate using the platform-specific methods below. Once authenticated, the shared API is available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
App Data folder visibilityDuplicationFile typesPathsToken refreshappProperties

The App Data folder is not shown to users. A user can only see the amount of space it takes up by going to drive.google.com and navigating to Settings » Manage apps.

Files and folders don't need unique names in Google Drive. To avoid confusing duplicates, CloudBridge does its best to prevent them: createFile(), createFolder(), moveFile() and moveFolder() first check the target folder and throw a ConflictException if a file/folder with the new name already exists.

Folders in Google Drive are just files, but with the mimetype application/vnd.google-apps.folder.

Google Drive doesn't have the concept of paths. Instead, every file has a list of "parent file IDs". In the past, there could be multiple, but now every file can have just one parent.

To offer a unified API, CloudBridge still builds a path for Drive files. It will contain the parent file ID and filename. For example, a nested folder could look like /A2vXis2oKtcHO/9xZDTanHiFcgg/ and a file inside a folder could be /9xZDTanHiFcgg/promotion.txt.

Passing in a deeper path on a file (for example /id1/id2/file.txt) has no effect, as only the last part (id2) is set as a parent to the file/folder.

When retrieving changes with getDelta(), Google Drive only reports the ID of deleted items. The path of a DeletedDeltaChange is therefore /<fileId>, so match deletions on itemId.

Google Drive differs per platform:

  • Android: a new token is requested from Google Identity Services silently. It doesn't tell when a token expires, so this only happens after a token is rejected. The new token is requested for the account in CloudAccessToken.account. If the user needs to grant access again, a NotAuthenticatedException is thrown; call GoogleDriveAuthenticator.authenticate() then.
  • Web: the implicit flow has no refresh token, so tokens can't be refreshed. Re-authenticate when a NotAuthenticatedException is thrown.

Apps that used to store data in Drive's appProperties can read them with getFileAppProperties(), to migrate that data:

val properties: Map<String, String> = service.getFileAppProperties(file.id)

This is a migration helper only. CloudBridge offers a unified API across services, so it doesn't support setting or managing these properties.

docs.title: Registration in Cloud Console
docs.text:
Info

Every platform needs to be registered in the Google Cloud Console as "OAuth 2.0 Client ID" with the correct type (e.g., iOS, Android, Web, Desktop).

docs.title: Authenticating
Cloud services
docs.text:
These subpages show how to authenticate on each platform, and any remarks/limitations of specific services.

Service Data in app folder Support Delta support Chunk size Dropbox 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 8 MB 4 Google Drive 📦 Not visible to users1 ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 10 MB 5 OneDrive 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 10 MB 6 WebDAV 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms2 ❌ No3 Not chunked
  • "All platforms" means Android, iOS, desktop (JVM) and web (JS/WASM).
  • "Chunk size" is the size of each part in which files larger than 10 MB are uploaded.

  1. "App data not visible" means the user will not see the app files when opening the cloud folder themselves (e.g. on user's desktop or in the web interface of Google Drive). More details. ↩

  2. WebDAV on web requires dealing with CORS. Some providers, like Fastmail, block requests from all domains. ↩

  3. You could keep the last result of a call and compare a new result manually to get delta support with WebDAV. ↩

  4. A multiple of 4 MB, as required by Dropbox. ↩

  5. A multiple of 256 KB, as required by Google Drive. ↩

  6. A multiple of 320 KB, as required by OneDrive. ↩

docs.title: ☁️ WebDAV
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.webDav(
    WebDavCredentials(
        serverUrl = "https://example.com/webdav",
        username = "your-username",
        password = "your-password"
    )
)

Then the shared API is available.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
Set up a deeplink filter inside AndroidManifest.xml:

<!-- OAuth redirect deep link: com.example.myapp://cloudbridge-auth -->
<intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="com.example.myapp" android:host="cloudbridge-auth" />
</intent-filter>

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. The recommended format for CloudBridge is com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth, where com.example.app matches your app's identifier, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.

Open the auth URL in a Custom Tab and capture the redirect. Then exchange the authorization code for a token:

// When user wants to authenticate:
val url = service.authenticate(
    redirectUri = "yourRedirectUri" // e.g. a custom scheme like "com.example://cloudbridge-auth"
)
CustomTabsIntent.Builder().build().launchUrl(context, url.toUri())

// In your Activity's onNewIntent (and onCreate), call:
val uri = intent.data ?: return
val token = service.completeAuthentication(
    redirectUri = "com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth", // Needs to match the uri passed into authenticate()
    intentUri = uri
)

Securely store the token and pass it to the constructor of the service to use it.

docs.title: Desktop
docs.text:
val authServer = LocalAuthenticationServer() // optional parameter: `port=8080`

// Build auth URL and open it in the browser
val url = service.authenticate(
    authServer = authServer,
    onSuccess = { token ->
        service.setToken(token)
        TODO("Store the token locally")
    }
)
openBrowser(url)

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. Since CloudBridge on desktop uses a loopback server, the URL will be http://localhost:8080 (or whichever port you specify).

docs.title: iOS
docs.text:
service.authenticate(
    redirectUri = "com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth" // change to your app
)?.let { token ->
    service.setToken(token)
    TODO("Store the token locally")
}

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. The recommended format for CloudBridge is com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth, where com.example.app matches your app's identifier, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
// Always call this:
val token = service.completeAuthentication(redirectUri = "yourRedirectUri")
if (token != null) {
    service.setToken(token)
}

// When user wants to authenticate:
val uri = service.authenticate(redirectUri = "yourRedirectUri")
window.location.href = uri

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. For example, https://example.com/cloudbridge-callback, where https://example.com matches your app's domain, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.
